portfolioYoyTrend.methodHintTitle: 3MMA (3-Month Moving Aggregate) = rolling 3-month revenue total vs. the same 3 months last year. We don't use single-month YoY because a single month is swayed by seasonality and a few large orders, too noisy to show a trend direction; 3MMA smooths that out and reacts earlier than a trailing-12-month YoY. Basis: erp_sales_order order date, 8 VIP accounts combined. Consecutive decline months = counting back from the latest month, how many months YoY has stayed negative; a positive month or missing prior-year data breaks the streak.

about.title: What this version does
about.subtitle: For anyone seeing this screen for the first time — what each card is saying, and how they connect.

s1.heading: Why one sentence pattern
s1.p1: This version boils "understanding a customer" down to one sentence pattern: two lines diverging — comparing two metrics to see which one is moving faster.
s1.p2: Learn it once, and it applies across all 12 customers and 5 cards each — no separate rulebook to memorize for each one.
s1.note: A card only points out where something is different; how to read it is left to whoever knows the customer best.

quality.title: Quality
quality.desc: Five metrics (DOA, RMA, CFQR, FPY, repair rate) against target. Status colors and thresholds follow the production system's rules.

sales.title: Sales
sales.desc: This year's scorecard, plus five clues.

s3.heading: The five clues form a causal chain — the order is fixed
s3.intro: These five cards run in a fixed order, from source to result:

item2.label: How much of it do we win?

item3.label: What do the orders look like?

s3.quote: Fewer orders is the outcome; pipeline is the source. So these five cards start from the source, not the outcome.

s4.heading: Card titles state only what's measured
s4.p1: Titles never assert customer or competitor intent, and never claim something we don't actually measure. "The customer is testing the waters" or "a competitor is eating share" are guesses, not things the data can prove — that inference is left to the viewer.
s4.p2: The "So what?" line under each card is a question, not a claim (e.g. "check whether the annual price negotiation ate the margin") — it isn't bound by this rule.
s4.p3: All three cases where the scorecard misses target are written the same way: "confirm the main gap with sales." There are too many possible reasons a target is missed (lead time, cost, capacity, FX...) — the data can only prove whether the target was hit, not why.

s5.heading: The same divergence means the opposite thing for different customers
s5.p1: Customers fall into two types: ODM Project accounts and Standard Product accounts (by ODM-model revenue share over the trailing 12 months, threshold 30%).
s5.example: For example, take "shipments catching up with orders":
s5.exampleOdm: for an ODM Project customer, it means a previously-won project is now shipping in volume (good news)
s5.exampleStd: for a Standard Product customer, it means old orders are being worked down with no new orders replacing them (worth watching)
s5.p2: So before reading a card, check which type this customer is — it's flagged at the top of the Sales tab.

s6.heading: Clues can be questioned further
s6.p1: The card gives a conclusion; the Q&A fills in what the card doesn't say.
s6.p2: All five clues have Q&A, two questions each. The button appears on cards that have Q&A.
s6.p3: Answers are generated by a local language model, using only the facts this clue itself computed — every sentence must trace back to that fact list. Nothing leaves the local network.

s7.heading: What's real and what's simulated
s7.p1: Every customer, order, deal, and quality number on screen is simulated data — none of it is a real customer.
s7.p2: Quality metric definitions and status thresholds follow the production system exactly; nothing was relaxed for the demo.
s7.p3: AI text is generated live by the local model. Pressing "Regenerate" runs it again — wording changes each time, but the underlying numbers don't.
s7.p4: AI summaries can be switched between Chinese, English, Japanese and Korean. Japanese and Korean are translated from the Chinese version, and the card is labeled "AI-translated, for reference only".

s8.heading: Home: all 12 VIP customers at a glance
s8.p1: The "AI Highlights" strip at the top is a carousel: the first slide is a cross-customer overview, followed by the quality and sales highlights of each of the 12 VIP customers. It advances every 30 seconds and can also be paged manually. "Regenerate" rewrites only the first, overview slide.
s8.p2: The top-right corner of the chart below switches between two views:
s8.quality: Quality risk distribution — RMA on the x-axis, DOA on the y-axis, bubble size is shipment volume. The further to the upper right, the higher the quality risk.
s8.growth: Growth matrix — the x-axis is the customer's share of company revenue; the y-axis is growth above or below the company average (percentage points); bubble size is the weighted pipeline value for the next 6 months. A 5% share and 0 relative growth divide the chart into four quadrants: Grow, Maintain, Nurture and Review. New customers this period have no prior-year comparison, so they are left out of the quadrants and noted below the chart.
s8.p3: From the Quality tab, select a model to see its RMA, CFQR, FPY, repair details and ranking.

tour.heading: Tour routes: pick one by available time
tour.intro: The three walkthroughs below go from brief to in-depth. Choose one based on how much time the audience has.

short.title: 30 seconds: the quick overview
short.body: This is a dashboard that helps sales managers keep track of their key accounts. The AI highlights at the top move to a new customer every 30 seconds, with a sentence or two on what needs attention this period. The chart below shows at a glance which customers carry quality risk, and switching to the growth matrix shows which ones merit more investment. The data on screen is simulated; quality thresholds are the same as the production system.

mid.title: 3 minutes: look at one customer
mid.step1: Home (about 1 minute): the AI highlights carousel → the quality risk distribution (the further upper right, the higher the risk) → switch to the growth matrix and look at the customers marked "★ Grow" in the upper right.
mid.step2: Open one customer (about 1 minute): for example 大和精機工業株式会社 (Grow quadrant, ODM Project type). The Quality tab shows the status lights for five metrics; the Sales tab shows the annual scorecard.
mid.step3: Wrap-up (about 30 seconds): every customer is read the same way, so learning it once covers all 12. AI summaries are generated by a local model, and no data leaves the company.

long.title: 10 minutes: in depth
long.intro: After the 3-minute version, add the following four points:
long.step1: The five clues form a causal chain: pipeline → wins → order mix → shipments → on-time delivery. Fewer orders is the outcome, so the analysis starts from the source, the pipeline.
long.step2: The same signal means the opposite for different customers: "shipments catching up with orders" is good news for an ODM customer but needs attention for a Standard Product customer. The customer type is shown at the top of the Sales tab.
long.step3: Live follow-up questions: click the Q&A button on a clue card. Answers are based only on the numbers computed for that clue and never reach the external internet.
long.step4: Languages and models: switch the summary to Japanese or Korean; from the Quality tab, open a model to see its RMA details.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: Can the AI say things that have no basis?
faq.a1: Card titles state only measurable facts and do not speculate about customer intent. "Suggested follow-up" is a question, not a conclusion.
faq.a2: All of it is simulated. Metric definitions and status thresholds follow the production system.
faq.q3: Why is the "Nurture" quadrant of the growth matrix empty?
faq.a3: In this period's simulated data, no customer has a small share with fast growth. The thresholds were not adjusted to fill the layout.
faq.q4: Does Regenerate give a different result every time?
faq.a4: The wording may differ; the underlying numbers do not change.
